draft.summary: The dataset contains 12,330 rows and 18 columns with no missing values and all contract checks passed. Duplicate rows were retained as they represent valid single-page bounce sessions from different users. Some month values were standardized for consistency, and the dataset includes a purchase rate of 15.5%, indicating class imbalance handled during modeling.

findings.title: Duplicate Rows Represent Valid Sessions
findings.detail: There are 125 identical rows in the raw data which were kept because they represent single-page bounce sessions from different users.
findings.why_it_matters: Retaining these duplicates ensures the dataset accurately reflects user behavior without artificially reducing data size, preserving model training quality.

findings.title: Month Values Standardized for Consistency
findings.detail: The month value 'June' was renamed to 'Jun' in 288 rows to maintain consistent categorical values across the dataset.
findings.why_it_matters: Consistent categorical values prevent errors in encoding and improve model interpretability and performance.

findings.title: No Missing Values and Contract Compliance
findings.detail: The dataset has zero missing values and passes all contract checks including presence of all 18 columns, 17 required features, numeric ranges within bounds, and categorical values within allowed values.
findings.why_it_matters: Complete and contract-compliant data ensures reliability and validity for downstream analysis and modeling.

findings.title: Class Imbalance Present in Purchase Sessions
findings.detail: Only 15.5% of sessions ended in a purchase, indicating an imbalanced target variable.
findings.why_it_matters: Class imbalance requires stratified splits and appropriate metrics like PR-AUC to ensure fair and effective model evaluation.

findings.title: Sessions with Zero Duration and Very Long Sessions Kept
findings.detail: 720 sessions have zero total time (single-page visits) and 78 sessions last over 3 hours; both were retained as the model uses robust trees.
findings.why_it_matters: Keeping these sessions preserves data diversity and allows the model to learn from all user behaviors without bias from outlier removal.

cleaning_explained: The month value 'June' was renamed to 'Jun' in 288 rows to standardize categorical data and avoid inconsistencies during analysis.
125 identical rows were kept because they represent valid single-page bounce sessions from different users, ensuring data completeness.
The final dataset shape remains 12,330 rows by 18 columns after cleaning, confirming no data loss occurred during processing.
